Resubmitted and accepted.

**T4C — deviation (fallback target), paragraph 4(a) [p0016]**

What changed from the first pass: the Customer convenience right is now carried in operative language inside the edit rather than relied on as an already-met quote from the sentence being replaced. The single replace:

- States our right expressly: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient." (fallback 60–90 day window)
- Confines Kubient: "Kubient may terminate this Agreement upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer, effective only at the end of the then-current Term." — this both ties the effective date to a term boundary (per the verifier's tightening note) and keeps the 90-day notice floor.
- Early-termination-fee element remains already met by the untouched fee sentence (Kubient takes only fees generated in the 90-day run-off).
- The Initial Term lock-out sentence, 4(b) breach/insolvency rights, the auto-renewal mechanic and the fee sentence are retained verbatim; preferred wording (30 days, pro-rata refund) is not pursued because the fallback is reached.
